briefs.headline: Crude oil outlook: US-Iran talks, supply risks likely to keep prices volatile
briefs.deck: As talks between the US and Iran unfold regarding the strategic Strait of Hormuz, crude oil prices are poised for fluctuations. Market experts suggest that a successful diplomatic resolution might lower prices, though persistent regional tensions could sustain high levels. Recent geopolitical conflicts have already strained supply chains, raising shipping costs.
briefs.bodyText:
Crude oil prices are expected to witness sharp fluctuations next week as investors assess the prospects of a US-Iran agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz against the risk of further supply disruptions in Middle East. Analysts said any diplomatic breakthrough could bring prices down, although continued restrictions on oil shipments and escalating regional tensions may limit the decline.
"Crude oil is caught between diplomatic optimism and persistent physical supply risks. MCX crude holding above Rs 8,500, against pre-war levels near Rs 6,500, highlights the significant supply-risk premium still embedded in prices," Navneet Damani, Head of Research - Commodities at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said, as quoted by PTI.
The direction of prices will largely depend on developments in Washington and Tehran. US President Donald Trump has described negotiations as constructive and said Washington would not launch a military strike against Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. Iran, meanwhile, is evaluating the US response to its proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Analysts believe a positive response from Tehran could trigger a near-term correction in oil prices. 
However, uncertainty over the restoration of supplies through the strategic waterway is likely to keep a geopolitical risk premium in place.
"Globally, developments around US-Iran diplomacy and crude oil prices will remain critical. Any progress on a framework for reopening the Strait of Hormuz could ease energy prices and provide some relief to India’s import bill and the rupee, while renewed geopolitical tensions could keep volatility elevated," Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research, Religare Broking, said.
The Strait of Hormuz remains severely constrained, with September's improvement in oil exports largely supported by alternative shipping routes. Damani noted that these routes remain expensive, stretched and vulnerable to further disruption, suggesting that even a diplomatic breakthrough may not immediately restore normal supply conditions.
Further uncertainty has emerged following Trump's remarks that the US was considering joining Saudi strikes against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen after an attack on Riyadh's international airport.
"The widening conflict has heightened concerns over energy shipments through the region, including the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait," Damani said.
According to Choice Broking, attacks on 11 tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have pushed freight rates to record highs and created severe shipping bottlenecks. Any further disruption to these routes could keep crude prices elevated in the coming sessions.
Meanwhile, traders will also assess the impact of hurricane-related production shutdowns in the US Gulf of Mexico. The disruptions supported West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude prices towards the end of last week, although that support could weaken as production resumes.
Damani said global supply expectations continued to be revised lower, with a meaningful recovery in Gulf supplies uncertain before 2027.
On the data front, investors will closely follow the monthly oil market reports from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and the International Energy Agency (IEA) for fresh estimates of global oil demand and supply.
Weekly crude inventory figures from the American Petroleum Institute, along with US government data on crude stocks and imports, will also provide direction to prices.
The market will additionally assess the impact of the US Treasury's temporary licence allowing Russia to release 22.5 million barrels of diesel into global markets. According to Choice Broking, the measure helped limit price gains, while diplomatic de-escalation discussions involving Western allies and Ukraine in Miami provided some relief.
Crude oil prices ended the previous week with mixed movements. Brent futures for December delivery rose $2.47, or 2.41 per cent, to $104.72 per barrel, while WTI gained 1 per cent to settle at USD 91.85 per barrel.
In the domestic market, October crude futures on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) declined Rs 35, or 0.4 per cent, to Rs 8,881 per barrel. The November contract gained Rs 82, or nearly 1 per cent, to Rs 8,828 per barrel.
With Brent trading above $100 per barrel, analysts expect geopolitical developments to remain the dominant driver of oil prices next week. While progress in US-Iran negotiations could provide some relief, the risk of renewed attacks, shipping disruptions and prolonged supply constraints is likely to keep volatility elevated.

briefs.headline: Inflation data, IT earnings, crude oil to steer stock markets this week, say experts
briefs.deck: Anticipation is high in Indian stock markets as volatility and consolidation loom, particularly with September's inflation data on the horizon. These figures will shed light on price movements and may sway the Reserve Bank of India's policy decisions. The week also promises notable quarterly earnings from key corporations, adding another layer of influence on market behavior.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Indian stock markets are likely to remain volatile and consolidate this week as investors track September inflation data, quarterly earnings from major companies, crude oil prices and global economic cues. Foreign investor flows, rupee movements, US Treasury yields and geopolitical developments will also influence sentiment, analysts said.
After eight consecutive weeks of declines, the Nifty-50 gained 0.43 per cent last week, while the Sensex rose 0.78 per cent, signalling some stabilisation. However, elevated crude oil prices and continued foreign institutional investor (FII) selling could limit the recovery.
“Indian equities are expected to consolidate this week as markets balance improving domestic earnings momentum against elevated global risks. Brent crude remains above USD 100 per barrel and sustained FII selling continues to weigh on sentiment. After eight consecutive weeks of declines, the Nifty-50 gained 0.4 per cent last week, suggesting some stabilisation at lower levels, although the broader market is likely to remain selective,” Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said, as quoted by PTI.
Inflation data in focus
Investors will closely track India's September consumer price index (CPI) and wholesale price index (WPI) inflation figures for clues about price pressures and the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy outlook.
“September CPI inflation will be the first major domestic test this week. A stronger-than-expected reading could revive concerns over further RBI tightening, putting rate-sensitive sectors such as banking, automobiles and real estate under pressure while raising the risk of a broader drag on consumer demand.
“A softer print could ease concerns over the eventual peak in interest rates, but any relief may prove short-lived if Brent crude remains above USD 100 a barrel. Wholesale price inflation data will offer a further indication of how elevated energy and logistics costs are filtering through to producer prices,” Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder and CEO of HST Wealth, said.
Global economic indicators will add to the market cues, with US inflation and retail sales data likely to influence Treasury yields and the dollar. Investors will also monitor eurozone inflation and UK GDP data, alongside developments in the global jobs market.
IT earnings to set the tone
The September-quarter earnings season will gather pace this week, with results from HCL Technologies, Wipro and Tech Mahindra among the likely key triggers for the market. Investors will look for signs of sustained demand, deal momentum and management guidance to assess whether the recent recovery in IT stocks can continue.
IT shares led Friday's market rebound, with TCS rallying more than 4 per cent after reporting better-than-expected September-quarter results. The gains helped lift the broader indices after weeks of pressure.
The sector had also faced concerns following reports that the US suspended eight IT firms, including TCS, Infosys, Wipro, Cognizant and Microsoft, from a programme linked to green card applications for foreign workers. The programme's critics have argued that it disadvantages American workers.
TCS said on Friday that the US action was not expected to affect its workforce strategy or customer engagements. The company cited the small number of applications it had made under the programme over the past two years and its focus on local hiring.
“The IT sector will remain in focus as HCL Technologies, Wipro and Tech Mahindra report their September quarter results. The sector staged a sharp rebound on Friday following TCS's better-than-expected earnings, but whether the recovery gains traction will depend on the performance of its peers and their outlook for the coming quarters,” Radhakrishnan said.
Other companies scheduled to announce results this week include BHEL, Canara Bank, HDB Financial Services, HDFC Asset Management Company and Nestle.
Crude oil and geopolitical risks remain key concerns
Crude oil prices will remain a major macroeconomic factor for Indian equities, given the country's exposure to imported energy. Brent crude trading above USD 100 per barrel could add to inflationary pressures, weigh on corporate margins and complicate the outlook for interest rates.
Uncertainty surrounding Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and regional energy infrastructure has kept concerns over potential supply disruptions elevated.
“Corporate earnings will increasingly influence sector-level performance as the September quarter results season gathers pace. TCS’s results helped trigger a rebound across IT stocks, supporting the broader indices on Friday. Crude oil remains the biggest macroeconomic risk. Uncertainty over Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and regional energy infrastructure continues to leave global supply vulnerable to disruption,” Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said.
Alongside oil prices, investors will monitor foreign institutional investor activity, movements in the rupee and US Treasury yields for indications of capital flows and broader risk appetite.

stories.headline: After 15 years, India's tailender achieves rare T20I feat
stories.deck: Prince Yadav has joined S Sreesanth and Ravichandran Ashwin on a rare list of Indian batters after hitting three fours against the West Indies in the third T20I in Indore on Sunday. He became only the third Indian batter batting at No. 10 or No. 11 to hit at least three boundaries in a T20 International.
stories.bodyText:
Prince Yadav has joined 
S Sreesanth
 and 
Ravichandran Ashwin
 on a rare list of Indian batters after hitting three fours against the West Indies in the third T20I in Indore on Sunday. He became only the third Indian batter batting at No. 10 or No. 11 to hit at least three boundaries in a T20 International.
The feat came after a gap of 15 years, with Ashwin being the last Indian batter to achieve it in 2011. Prince's late contribution also helped India reach 223 before the hosts secured a 14-run victory to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.
Prince joins Sreesanth and Ashwin
Sreesanth tops the list with four boundaries against New Zealand in Johannesburg in 2007. Ashwin hit three fours against England in Kolkata in 2011, while Prince matched his tally against the West Indies in Indore in 2026.
Prince's achievement came 19 years after Sreesanth's effort and 15 years after Ashwin's innings.
Most boundaries by an Indian No. 10 or No. 11 in a T20I
Three boundaries in the final over
Prince came out to bat in the 19th over with India at 202/8. With wickets falling towards the end of the innings, he made the most of his opportunity by hitting three fours off Shamar Joseph.
He opened his account with a boundary through deep mid-wicket off a low full toss. Two balls later, he read the delivery well and scooped it over wicketkeeper Shai Hope for another four.
Prince then got a thick top edge off a short-of-length delivery, which flew over short third man to give him his third boundary of the over. He also ran a bye during the over as the West Indies players questioned the umpire's decision.
His quick scoring helped India add useful runs at a crucial stage and finish with 223.
India bowlers seal 14-run win
Abhishek Sharma had laid the foundation for India's total with a 30-ball 69, while Ishan Kishan contributed 37 off just 18 deliveries. However, India's progress slowed after a series of wickets in the second half of the innings.
The bowlers made sure those late setbacks did not prove costly. Arshdeep Singh picked up three wickets for 44 runs, while Naman Dhir claimed two as the West Indies finished on 209/7.
Shamar Springer gave the visitors hope with an unbeaten 35 off just 11 balls, but India held on for a 14-run win.
The victory put India 2-1 ahead in the five-match series.
The fourth T20I will be played in Hyderabad on Wednesday.

stories.headline: 'Let them do whatever': Shami breaks silence on continued India snubs
stories.deck: Mohammed Shami has been out of favour with the national selectors, but he said he would continue playing wherever he gets an opportunity instead of worrying about his return to the Indian team. The Bengal fast bowler made the remarks after taking four wickets against Delhi in Bengal's opening match of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season in Kalyani on Sunday. His figures of 4/30 helped Bengal bowl…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Mohammed Shami
 has responded to questions about his fitness and bowling rhythm, saying he is focused on playing cricket rather than paying attention to outside comments.
The Bengal fast bowler made the remarks after taking four wickets against Delhi in Bengal's opening match of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season in Kalyani on Sunday. His figures of 4/30 helped Bengal bowl Delhi out for 240 on the first day.
The 36-year-old has been out of favour with the national selectors, but he said he would continue playing wherever he gets an opportunity instead of worrying about his return to the Indian team.
'It doesn't bother me'
Shami said people were free to comment on his fitness and performances, but he would continue to focus on his game.
"People perhaps enjoy looking and passing comments more. They say the rhythm isn't there, that he doesn't look fit, or whatever else. It doesn't bother me. I'm on the ground, I'm playing, and I'm playing wherever I'm given a chance. The rest is your job," Shami said during a press conference.
The fast bowler was once again left out of India's squad, this time for the T20I series against New Zealand. The selection also marked the return of 
Bhuvneshwar Kumar
 to the national team after a gap of four years.
Asked about his own omission, Shami said he no longer wanted to comment on selection decisions and would concentrate on playing cricket.
"I have stopped making such comments. It makes no difference to me. Now, whoever wants to do whatever, let them. My job is just to play," he added.
Shami hails Bhuvneshwar's return
Shami also supported the decision to bring Bhuvneshwar back into India's T20I squad. He said the experienced pacer's return should encourage other players to keep working hard and believing in their abilities.
The Bengal pacer stressed that talented players who continue to perform should not be kept out of the team for long periods.
"A person should keep going on hope alone," Shami said.
"Look at the skill he has. It's not as if he hasn't been talking to anyone or anything like that. That doesn't mean you should keep a talent out for a long time. I'm happy for him because this has come after such a long time. He has also delivered performances consistently in the IPL. If someone is working hard, showing their skill and has the potential, why shouldn't they be playing? Everyone deserves a chance to perform."
Shami's comments came as he continued to make his case through performances in domestic cricket. He said he remained motivated to play for as long as he wanted to continue his career.
Four wickets put Bengal in control
Shami backed up his words with a strong performance against Delhi in the Ranji Trophy opener.
After Bengal elected to bowl, their pace attack made good use of the movement available on the pitch. Shami led the effort with four wickets for 30 runs, while Akash Deep took two wickets for 74 runs and Mukesh Kumar claimed one for 43.
Off-spinner Amir Ghani also played an important role, taking three wickets for 45 runs.
Shami dismissed Yash Dhull, Ayush Doseja, Hrithik Shokeen and Divij Mehra. Shokeen was Delhi's top scorer, making 56 off 98 balls, before Shami removed him.
Delhi were eventually bowled out for 240 in 77.3 overs, giving Bengal a strong start to their campaign.
With another impressive domestic performance, Shami showed that he remains focused on proving himself on the field rather than responding to questions about his fitness or selection.

stories.headline: Premier League: Man City defeats Liverpool 3-0, silencing hostile Anfield crowd
stories.deck: Haaland, Doku and Cherki score for Manchester City as league leader maintains perfect start to season
stories.bodyText:
Manchester City silenced a hostile Anfield crowd as second-half goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki secured a 3-0 victory over 10-man Liverpool on Sunday (October 12, 2026) and maintained the Premier League leaders' perfect start to the season.
City were playing for the first time since an independent commission found them guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, and were greeted by deafening boos and angry chants.
But Enzo Maresca's side stood firm against Liverpool's early pressure and a fevered atmosphere before taking control after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off in the 62nd minute for a second booking following a foul on Doku.
Haaland sparks rout for City
Haaland then struck three minutes later, smashing a left-footed shot past Alisson after Doku worked the ball into the box and his attempted shot was deflected into the path of the big Norwegian.
Haaland made a beeline to celebrate with the travelling City fans including Oasis frontman Noel Gallagher.
Doku doubled the lead in the 68th minute with a gorgeous long-range shot that curled into the far top corner. Cherki completed the rout and sent scores of Liverpool fans heading to the exits -- in the 78th minute when he let the ball roll through to Josko Gvardiol before turning into the box to meet his teammate's pass and slot the ball home.
"It was a lovely moment that will stay with us a long time," Man City striker Haaland told Sky Sports.
"It’s time to stay strong and stick together and do what you can do something about, stick together."
Man City midfielder Elliot Anderson said City's unity had stood out.
"We've shown real togetherness and fight. It's a tough place to come and it's challenging," he said.
"We really stuck together out there, fought for each other and played well."
The Liverpool fans left at the final whistle chanted "Going down! Going Down! Going Down!" in reference to City's potential relegation. The club have denied all wrongdoing, and have appealed the independent commission's verdict.
City delivers defiant response
A defiant Haaland and Maresca grinned and pumped their fists at the City fans, who delightedly waved inflatable bananas, a tradition dating from their time out of the top flight in the 1980s.
The victory gave City six wins from six and moved them three points clear of Arsenal on 18 points, providing a forceful response on the pitch after a turbulent week away from it. Liverpool are ninth after their first league loss of the season.
Maresca is only the fourth manager to win their first six Premier League matches in charge of a club, after Pep Guardiola (City in 2016), Carlo Ancelotti (Chelsea, 2009) and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (Manchester United, 2018-19).
City's resounding victory comes with caveats. While they remain firmly in control at the top of the league, their perfect start increasingly stands in contrast to the uncertainty surrounding the club, with the fallout from the financial rules verdict leaving far more questions than answers about what comes next.

stories.headline: Focus on my game and consistency helped me make a comeback, says Karan
stories.bodyText:
Karan Lamba, who announced himself with an unbeaten century on his Ranji Trophy debut in 2023, last played for Rajasthan in the competition in February 2024. He marked his return to the side with an unbeaten 103 against Tamil Nadu here on Sunday.
The 21-year-old said he continued to focus on his performances in the u-23 circuit during his two-year absence from the Ranji side, knowing that an opportunity could come at any time.
“I focused on my game and tried to perform as consistently as possible in u-23 cricket. You never know when selectors might pick you, so I never took any match lightly. The only thing was that the u-23 matches do not get as much live coverage, so you are not always in the limelight. But I believe that if you perform well, the selectors keep an eye on you, irrespective of the level you play at,” he said.
Karan was Rajasthan’s highest run-getter in the Vijay Hazare Trophy last season. He said it gave him the confidence that a Ranji opportunity would follow. “I felt I had established my place and felt I would get an opportunity the following season. That allowed me to focus on how I could take my game to the next level,” he said.
Karan said he was determined to make the most of Sunday’s good batting surface and convert his start into a substantial score.
“The wicket was very good (for batting), and you rarely get such flat tracks. I wanted to make the most of the opportunity and bat for as long as possible,” he said.

briefs.headline: 'West Indies, you can never take them lightly': Shreyas Iyer after India take 2-1 lead
briefs.deck: India captain Shreyas Iyer praised his bowlers for their confident approach and clear plans after the team defeated the West Indies by 14 runs in the third T20I at Holkar Stadium on Sunday. The victory gave India a 2-1 lead in the five-match series. India successfully defended a target of 224, restricting the West Indies to 209/7. Arshdeep Singh took three wickets, while Naman Dhir picked up two…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India captain 
Shreyas Iyer
 praised his bowlers for their confident approach and clear plans after the team defeated the West Indies by 14 runs in the third T20I at Holkar Stadium on Sunday. The victory gave India a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.
India successfully defended a target of 224, restricting the West Indies to 209/7. Arshdeep Singh took three wickets, while Naman Dhir picked up two scalps to help India stop the visitors from completing another successful chase.
Iyer impressed with bowlers' approach
Iyer said the bowlers knew what they wanted to do and backed themselves to execute their plans under pressure.
"It was wonderful because the bowlers were pretty confident with what they wanted to execute. The clarity was much more visible. They were decisive in their execution and when I was passing the ball to them, each and every bowler was up for the challenge and that's what you want," Iyer said during the post-match presentation.
Arshdeep played a key role in the defence, finishing with figures of 3/44. He dismissed in-form opener Shai Hope early and later removed Keemo Paul and Sherfane Rutherford in the 18th over to put India firmly in control.
Dhir also made an important contribution with two wickets, including the dismissal of Kamil Pooran, who had threatened to turn the game around with an aggressive innings.
Iyer praises Abhishek and Kishan
India's strong start with the bat came from 
Abhishek Sharma
 and Ishan Kishan. Abhishek smashed 69 off 30 balls, while Kishan scored 37 off just 18 deliveries.
Iyer praised both batters for giving India momentum at the top of the order. He also highlighted Prince Yadav's contribution towards the end of the innings.
"Honestly, that was a phenomenal start. Abhishek doing what he does in the powerplay and Kishan coming in. He's been great in the last few months. Even Prince (Yadav) playing the cameo in the end, those were crucial runs.
"West Indies, you can never take them lightly. So, we had to make sure we never got complacent. These are high-scoring grounds but it's important to stick to our process and follow our routines and make sure we stay offensive," Iyer said.
Hetmyer and Pooran threaten India's defence
The West Indies began their chase with an early setback when Arshdeep bowled Shai Hope for one. However, Shimron Hetmyer counterattacked and made the most of a dropped catch by Abhishek Sharma at short third man.
Hetmyer struck boundaries against the Indian bowlers and scored 43 before being bowled by a slower delivery from Dhir.
Rovman Powell fell for five after attempting a big shot against Axar Patel. Pooran then attacked Dhir, hitting three sixes in an attempt to bring the West Indies back into the contest.
However, Dhir dismissed Pooran for 42 when the batter attempted another pick-up shot but failed to get enough elevation.
Arshdeep seals India's victory
Sherfane Rutherford and Quention Sampson tried to rebuild the innings with some aggressive batting. Sampson, however, was caught at long-off off Nitish Kumar Reddy.
Arshdeep then struck twice in four balls during the 18th over, dismissing Keemo Paul and Rutherford to leave the West Indies with too much to do.
Shamar Springer provided some late excitement with an unbeaten 35 off just 11 balls, but his effort was not enough to take the visitors over the line. The West Indies finished on 209/7, falling 14 runs short.
The result also marked the first victory for a team batting first in the white-ball series so far. India had looked set for a bigger total after Abhishek's explosive innings, but a series of soft dismissals in the second half of their innings had given the West Indies hope.
India's bowlers made sure that the late batting collapse did not cost the team the match, helping the hosts move ahead in the T20I series.

briefs.headline: ‘Virat Kohli was a bit bitter’: Ex-India cricketer drops big verdict
briefs.deck: Kohli's retirement came after months of uncertainty over his future in Test cricket.
briefs.bodyText:
Virat Kohli's retirement from Test cricket may have come as a surprise to many, but former India cricketer Wasim Jaffer believes the star batter was unhappy with how his exit was handled. Jaffer feels Kohli could have continued playing the longest format and said the circumstances surrounding his retirement could have been managed better.
“Yes, absolutely. I mean, it seemed like Virat was a bit bitter about how things were handled,” Jaffer said on his YouTube channel, as quoted by India Today.
“A player like Virat, he draws crowds to the stadium; he has such a massive following. He definitely could have played more Test cricket. Until we hear directly from Virat what the actual situation was, we won't know for sure.”
Kohli's retirement came after months of uncertainty over his future in Test cricket. The former India captain had been keen to continue playing the format and tour England. He had also represented Delhi in a Ranji Trophy match in January 2025, underlining his commitment to red-ball cricket.
However, the situation reportedly changed in April. Kohli was reportedly left disillusioned by the developments and later informed the selectors that he did not want to be part of the England tour. 
Attempts by people close to him and some BCCI officials to convince him to reconsider did not succeed.
Jaffer pointed to Kohli's preparations for the England tour as a reason to question how the situation had been handled.
“But I mean, he was preparing; he was gearing up for the England tour. So, all those things could have been handled better. As I said, regarding certain individuals, things could have been managed better,” Jaffer said.
Kohli announced his retirement from Test cricket on May 12, 2025, ending a 14-year career in the format. He scored 9,230 runs, including 30 centuries, in 123 Tests.

briefs.headline: Shami happy to see Bhuvneshwar back in the Indian team
briefs.bodyText:
Even at 36, Mohammed Shami stands out with his skill-set and hard work to underline his worth.
Having started his Ranji Trophy season well with a four-wicket haul for Bengal in its outing against Delhi at the Bengal Cricket Academy ground here on Sunday, Shami said he did not feel any difference about his ‘inbuilt skill.’
“You should have the smartness to know when to make the ball move in and out. I don’t feel any change (about my performance). People express their opinions, such as I don’t have the rhythm and fitness. I don’t care about all this and I enjoy my game,” said Shami, leading the Bengal attack, also comprising international pacers Akash Deep and Mukesh Kumar.
Shami parried a question on whether he had contacted the National selectors, but spoke about his fitness. “You people (reporters) can see and write. I am inside the ground and am playing,” said Shami, while expressing his happiness over fellow pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s India selection after four years.
On Bengal’s ongoing match, Shami reiterated his demand that the home team should get a favourable track instead of a slow one. “We wanted a helpful pitch. No other team has such a fast bowling attack in India. We have requested many times. I don’t think there is a response.
“It was humid. You have to work smartly. When you don’t get help from the pitch, I don’t think there’s any smartness in putting in long spells and finishing one’s energy. I had planned for everyone,” said Shami.

briefs.headline: Erling Haaland’s Abu Dhabi home opens two routes to UAE’s 10-year Golden Visa
briefs.deck: Erling Haaland’s new Abu Dhabi home has raised questions about whether the Manchester City striker could secure a 10-year UAE Golden Visa through property investment or his sporting achievements. With a separate residency pathway for elite athletes and strong ties to Abu Dhabi through City, Haaland has several potential routes to explore, although no visa approval or special arrangement has been…
briefs.bodyText:
Erling Haaland
’s new home in Abu Dhabi puts the Manchester City striker in a position where securing a 10-year UAE Golden Visa could be a straightforward step if he chooses to pursue it. Given his status as one of football’s biggest stars, his achievements on the pitch and his ties to an Abu Dhabi-backed club, he could also be considered for a Golden Visa through special recognition rather than relying solely on the property investment route. While there has been no official announcement that Haaland has been granted the visa, his profile makes him a natural candidate for such an opportunity. However, he has not publicly expressed any intention or ambition to pursue UAE residency.
Haaland’s new Abu Dhabi home puts a 10-year visa within reach
Haaland announced his property purchase today through a video shared by the developers, revealing that he and his father, former Manchester City player Alf-Inge Haaland, had bought homes in the Manchester City Ohana project in Abu Dhabi. The development, created in collaboration with real estate company Ohana Residences, brings the club’s branding into a luxury waterfront community on Yas Island.
“Hi everyone, I’m so happy because I’m joining the Manchester City Ohana project. We will be neighbours in Abu Dhabi…I just got a house and so did my father,” Haaland said at the project’s launch event at the Etihad Arena.
The development offers townhouses, duplexes, and villas with prices starting above AED 3,600,000 ($1.02 million) for an average two-bedroom townhouse. 
A five-bedroom waterfront villa is expected to cost approximately $2.91 million, while bespoke estates reportedly start at $9.95 million.
The project also includes a Manchester City Training Academy, a City Lounge, and recreational facilities, while more than half of its master plan is dedicated to green spaces. Haaland’s exact property and purchase price have not been disclosed, but the development’s reported price range puts its residences above the UAE’s AED 2 million ($544,500) property-investment threshold.
The property naturally open the door to long-term residency in the UAE, adding another potential benefit to Haaland’s latest investment. Whether a Golden Visa forms part of the package or something he chooses to pursue separately, his new Abu Dhabi home adds to his growing ties to the country.
What the UAE Golden Visa offers beyond a property purchase
The Golden Visa is a long-term UAE residency programme designed to attract investors, entrepreneurs, skilled professionals, and people with exceptional talent. Under the current federal programme, eligible applicants can obtain renewable residency for 10 years without requiring a local sponsor, giving them greater independence from the employer-linked arrangements associated with conventional residency permits.
The programme allows qualifying residents to live, work, study and invest in the UAE, while extending residency opportunities to their families. Its main benefits include:
- Long-term residency: A renewable 10-year permit provides greater continuity than shorter-term residence arrangements.
- Family sponsorship: Holders can obtain residence permits for their spouses, children regardless of age and parents, as well as sponsor domestic workers under applicable regulations.
- Greater independence: Residents do not need an employer or another local sponsor to maintain their Golden Visa status.
- Flexible travel: Holders can remain outside the UAE for longer than the usual six-month absence limit that applies to many other residence visas.
- An entry period for overseas applicants: Eligible applicants outside the country can receive a six-month multiple-entry visa, renewable for another six months, while completing their residency procedures.
The programme serves several different categories, including property investors, entrepreneurs, scientists, outstanding students, and exceptional talents. Each pathway has its own eligibility rules, meaning applicants do not necessarily need to purchase expensive real estate to obtain long-term residency.
How Haaland’s property purchase could qualify him
Abu Dhabi’s official guidance for real estate investors sets a minimum qualifying property value of AED 2 million ($544,500), with ownership and investment documentation required as part of the application. Applicants may combine eligible properties to reach the threshold, while mortgages through national banks can be accepted when the investor’s qualifying capital remains at least AED 2 million ($544,500).
The requirements also distinguish between completed properties and off-plan purchases, which is particularly relevant for a newly launched development such as Manchester City Ohana Residences. For off-plan property, the applicant must provide a purchase agreement from an approved developer and evidence that at least AED 2 million ($544,500) has already been paid towards the property.
Although the development’s homes would qualify buyers for a 10-year Golden Visa, Haaland’s exact unit, payment arrangements and application status remain undisclosed, largely because the project is still being developed.
For Haaland, the property-investment route is the obvious starting point following his Abu Dhabi purchase. However, even without his new home, the UAE has an established traditional pathway for athletes to obtain a Golden Visa, meaning his achievements and standing in football could provide another route to long-term residency should he wish to pursue it.
The athlete pathway could make the property investment unnecessary
Abu Dhabi’s Golden Visa programme includes a 10-year residency category for athletes under its broader provision for outstanding talent. The official criteria focus on exceptional sporting ability and achievements, while the application process requires evidence that supports the applicant’s standing in their field.
An athlete applying through Abu Dhabi’s published route must provide:
- A sporting résumé documenting achievements and experience in their discipline.
- Supporting certificates or experience letters confirming those sporting accomplishments.
- A recommendation from Abu Dhabi Sports Council, which is the key formal endorsement in the published process.
Applications submitted through the Abu Dhabi Residents Office’s online system are automatically forwarded to the sports council for nomination, while applicants can also submit through the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security.
However, Haaland may not need to go through the usual nomination process to make a compelling case. As one of the most feared strikers of his generation and a global football superstar with a larger-than-life profile, his credentials speak for themselves. Should he wish to pursue the athlete route, his record would be difficult to overlook. To put that into context, Haaland could point to his Champions League triumph, multiple Premier League Golden Boot awards and standing among the world's elite footballers as evidence of his sporting achievements.
Crucially, the UAE's published athlete pathway does not require the AED 2 million ($544,500) property investment threshold. Eligible athletes can instead seek residency based on their sporting credentials, subject to the relevant authority's assessment and approval.
 Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi connection adds another dimension
Haaland’s situation is particularly interesting given Manchester City’s deep-rooted ties to Abu Dhabi. The club’s majority owner, Newton Investment and Development LLC, is wholly owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE’s Vice-President and Deputy Prime Minister. Since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008, City’s relationship with the emirate has grown considerably, and the partnership with Ohana Residences has now brought that connection into the property market.
Haaland is no ordinary player in this arrangement. As one of Manchester City’s biggest stars and the face of a development carrying the club’s name, he occupies a position of enormous commercial value. It is easy to see why his new home could be viewed as more than a property purchase, particularly given the UAE’s interest in attracting some of the biggest names in global sport and entertainment. One could even imagine a purchase of this nature being accompanied by residency arrangements, although no such package has been publicly confirmed in Haaland’s case.
Over the years, the UAE has attracted and welcomed prominent athletes, sporting personalities, actors, scientists and other internationally recognised figures, offering long-term residency opportunities to people whose achievements and expertise align with its ambitions. 
Against that backdrop, Haaland would have an exceptionally compelling case to present. His Champions League success, Premier League Golden Boot awards and status as one of the most recognisable footballers of his generation would make him a standout candidate under the country's athlete pathway.
Whether through his Abu Dhabi property or recognition of his sporting achievements, Haaland has a strong basis to explore long-term UAE residency should he wish to do so. His credentials make a persuasive case, even though no Golden Visa grant or special arrangement has been publicly announced.

briefs.headline: IND vs WI 3rd T20: Abhishek, Arshdeep to the fore as India wins a batathon to go 2-1 up
briefs.deck: The Men in Blue breached the 200-run mark yet again, recording 223 courtesy of opener Abhishek Sharma’s blast (69, 30b, 6x4, 5x6)
briefs.bodyText:
After the batathon in Ranchi, it was Indore’s turn to celebrate a festival of runs.
But this time though, the result was different. At the Holkar Stadium possessing pocket-sized boundaries, India kept intact its spectacular four-year streak of not losing back-to-back T20Is on home soil as it defeated the West Indies by 14 runs on Sunday.
Asked to set a target, the Men in Blue breached the 200-run mark yet again, recording 223 courtesy of opener Abhishek Sharma’s blast (69, 30b, 6x4, 5x6). While the West Indies batters kept themselves within touching distance for most part of the chase, they eventually could not pull off an encore, their pursuit ending at 209 for seven.
That the red-hot Shai Hope fell cheaply – missed one completely from Arshdeep Singh (three for 44) to have his stumps rearranged – did not help the Caribbean outfit’s cause.
Naman Dhir (two for 39) did the job with his secondary skill by removing set batters Shimron Hetmyer and Kamil Pooran. The off-spinner removed Hetmyer after the ball deflected off the southpaw’s pads and onto the stumps and had the last laugh against Kamil in a phase that included three sixes from the opener.
Earlier, Abhishek’s street-smart approach in the PowerPlay paid rich dividends.
The left-hander, who had been dismissed in his 20s by off-spinner Roston Chase in the first two games, had a few sighters before going on the rampage. The 26-year-old showed once again why he is the ‘Dada of off-side’ in the shortest format, making enough room to find and clear the boundary between sweeper cover and long-off with elan.
Abhishek was the protagonist in the 108-run second-wicket alliance (40 balls) with Ishan Kishan, which followed the early departure of Sanju Samson. But once Chase inflicted a double blow on the home side with the scalps of Kishan and skipper Shreyas Iyer in the ninth over, the visiting team marched right back into the contest.
By striking at regular intervals – the Men in Blue went from 115 for one to 223 all out – West Indies did not allow India to operate in the gear that Abhishek drove at. The stretch included the punishment imposed on Tilak Varma in the 17th over, by when Shreyas and Co. lost all their frontline batters.
The casual attitude and not-so-great phase, however, did not haunt India in the end as the host went 2-1 up in the five-game series.

briefs.headline: Abhishek, Arshdeep help India beat West Indies by 14 runs; take 2-1 lead in series
briefs.deck: In an exciting clash, India triumphed over West Indies by 14 runs in the third T20I match. Abhishek Sharma showcased his batting prowess with a swift 69 off 30 balls, propelling India to a formidable target of 224 runs. Despite valiant efforts from Shimron Hetmyer and Kamil Pooran, the West Indies fell short at 209 runs. Arshdeep Singh's remarkable bowling performance, capturing three wickets…
briefs.bodyText:
INDORE: A brilliant bowling display by India on a flat pitch with shorter boundaries at the Holkar Stadium guided them to a 14-run win over the West Indies and gave them a 2-1 lead in the series on Sunday.
With dew not coming into play in the third T20I, India's bowlers showcased their capabilities when the contest between bat and ball was evenly poised. They were on the money on most occasions, executed their plans perfectly and did not get rattled when the West Indies batters threatened to take the game away. In the end, the visitors were restricted to 209/7 while chasing a target of 224.
It began up front when Mayank Yadav (0/34) bowled all his deliveries above 145 kmph, hurrying the batters and conceding just two runs in his opening over. In the next over, West Indies skipper Shai Hope (5, 5b; 1x4) tried to force the pace but was cleaned up by Arshdeep Singh (3/44).
The West Indies then settled into a nice rhythm. They were not scoring at the rate India had managed in the Powerplay, but were doing enough to stay within touching distance of the required rate. Their charge was led by Shimron Hetmyer (43, 26b; 6x4, 2x6), who took the attack to the Indian bowlers. 
The left-hander had just taken 10 runs off two balls in the seventh over bowled by Naman Dhir (2/39), but on the very next delivery the off-spinner bowled a quicker ball with a flat trajectory that skidded on and rattled the stumps.
The dismissal stalled the visitors' scoring rate and they needed regular boundaries to stay in touch with the chase. Rovman Powell (5, 7b), who was struggling to get going, tried to force the issue but could only hit an Axar Patel (1/33) delivery straight down the throat of Ishan Kishan at deep mid-wicket. In the next over, Kamil Pooran (42, 27b; 3x4, 3x6) hit Dhir for three sixes before the Punjab all-rounder had him caught in the deep.
India then bowled a series of tight overs through Prince Yadav (0/37), Nitish Kumar Reddy (1/19) and Arshdeep, pushing the required rate up to 15 an over. The visitors gave it their all, but the target ultimately proved too steep.
Earlier, India were bowled out for 223 and owed much to the 108-run second-wicket partnership between Abhishek Sharma (69, 30b; 6x4, 5x6) and Ishan Kishan (37 18b; 6x4, 1x6), which came off just 40 deliveries and laid the platform for a total beyond 200.
Uncertain about whether dew would come into play, India could not afford to take their foot off the pedal. However, in their attempt to keep the scoring rate as high as possible, they lost their way through the middle overs. Perhaps memories of the West Indies chasing down 250 in the previous game weighed heavily on their minds after being put in to bat.
India managed just seven runs in the first two overs, with Sanju Samson (3, 6b) already back in the pavilion. But the floodgates opened thereafter as they added 80 runs in the next four overs to finish the Powerplay at 87/1. At one stage, they were cruising at 115/1 after 8.1 overs, with Abhishek and Ishan dispatching the West Indies bowlers all around the park.
Then came the twist that knocked the wind out of India's innings. The visitors tightened the screws, taking four wickets in the space of 16 balls to claw their way back into the contest.
As in the previous match, Roston Chase (2/38) used his cricketing nous to spark the fightback with two wickets in the ninth over. He first had Kishan stumped, a ball after being hit for a six, to end the pair's 108-run partnership. Two deliveries later, the off-spinner trapped skipper Shreyas Iyer lbw as the Indian captain looked to maintain the brisk scoring rate.
Five balls later, it was Abhishek's turn to depart after the left-hander skyed a short-of-a-length delivery from Shamar Springer (2/50). Naman Dhir (10, 5b; 1x4, 1x6) looked promising, launching Gudakesh Motie (1/37) over mid-on for six, but the left-arm spinner had the last laugh two balls later as the right-hander holed out at long-off.
India were suddenly reduced to 135/5 after 10.5 overs. The batters who followed got starts but failed to convert them into substantial contributions.

briefs.headline: Australia tighten grip on Durban Test, take 139-run lead after day 2
briefs.deck: Australia's bowlers shared the wickets as South Africa were dismissed for 284 in their first innings. Cummins finished with figures of 3/54, while Mitchell Starc (2/63), Josh Hazlewood (2/54) and Nathan Lyon (2/58) took two wickets each.
briefs.bodyText:
Pat Cummins
 picked up three wickets as Australia built a 139-run lead over South Africa by stumps on Day 3 of the first Test in Durban on Sunday.
Australia's bowlers shared the wickets as South Africa were dismissed for 284 in their first innings. Cummins finished with figures of 3/54, while 
Mitchell Starc
 (2/63), Josh Hazlewood (2/54) and Nathan Lyon (2/58) took two wickets each.
Australia had posted 390 in their first innings, with Matt Renshaw scoring a career-best 190 to help the visitors recover from 124/6.
Australia began their second innings and reached 33/0 in 5.4 overs before bad light forced another early end to the day's play. Nearly 13 overs were lost, with Nic Maddinson unbeaten on 17 and Travis Head on 10 at the crease.
David Bedingham top-scored for South Africa with 49 off 73 balls. The hosts were struggling at 197/8 before Keshav Maharaj and Simon Harmer added 52 runs for the ninth wicket to limit the damage. Maharaj made 34, while Harmer remained unbeaten on 35.
South Africa are the reigning World Test champions, having beaten Australia in the 2025 final. This is Australia's first tour of the country since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.
Cummins leads Australia's bowling effort
South Africa resumed Day 3 at 27/1 and reached 115/4 by lunch. 
Aiden Markram and Bedingham added 57 runs to their overnight partnership before Starc dismissed Markram for 37 in the 21st over, with the opener edging the ball to slip.
South Africa scored 59 runs for the loss of one wicket in the first hour. In the next session, captain Temba Bavuma fell for three while attempting a reverse sweep against Lyon. Steve Smith took the catch.
Cummins then dismissed Bedingham, who edged the ball to slip, where Smith took another catch, diving to his left.
After lunch, Cummins struck again to remove Wiaan Mulder for 30 off 50 balls, including three fours and a six. Mulder had added 56 runs with Tristan Stubbs before his dismissal.
Stubbs followed soon after for 32, caught at square leg off Cummins. Lyon then had Kyle Verreynne caught at slip for 13 as South Africa slipped to 197/7.
Marco Jansen struck six fours in a 20-ball 26 before he was caught off Hazlewood, leaving South Africa at 238/8 at tea.
Maharaj and Harmer kept the innings going and took South Africa past the follow-on mark with their ninth-wicket partnership. Their stand reached 52 before Starc dismissed Maharaj.

briefs.headline: Karan returns to Ranji Trophy in style, puts Rajasthan in control against TN
briefs.bodyText:
If Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot was a meditation on hope deferred, the opening day of the Elite Group-D Ranji Trophy match between Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan at the Sawai Mansingh Stadium here on Sunday was a story of opportunities seized when they finally arrived.
Karan Lamba struck an unbeaten 103 (135b, 11x4, 1x6) on his return to the Ranji Trophy after two years, debutant Rohan Rajbhar fell five runs short of a hundred (95, 220b, 13x4, 1x6), and Sumit Godara, drafted into the XI after Mukul Choudhary sustained an injury during the pre-match warm-up, made 49 as Rajasthan reached 286 for four. Tamil Nadu pacer P. Saravana Kumar, playing only his third Ranji match at 37, returned his best figures of three for 52.
Karan’s knock had a distinctly attacking streak. He struck three successive boundaries off debutant D. Deepesh - a square drive, a pull to long-on, and a cut - before charging Sai Kishore and lofting him over long-off for six to bring up his fifty off 45 balls. He completed his hundred off 133 balls with a back-foot square drive for four against Saravana Kumar.
Meanwhile, for 219 balls, Rohan negotiated the demands of first-class cricket with the composure of someone who had been there before. But with a maiden hundred beckoning tantalisingly, he gloved Saravana Kumar through to the keeper, walking off the field reluctantly.
Though his innings was restrained, there were moments of adventure. Rohan stepped out to loft Sai Kishore over long-on for six, then charged him again two balls later to drive straight for four. He also brought out the sweep for a four off the left-arm spinner. He was dropped on 80 when Sai Sudharsan put down an edge at first slip off medium-pacer Nidhish Rajagopal.
Rohan added 104 runs for the second wicket with Sumit and 125 for the third with Karan.
Tamil Nadu suffered a potential setback when all-rounder Sonu Yadav hobbled off after going down at backward point while attempting to stop a cut from Mahipal Lomror.
